senses.definition_en: Any of the four diacritical marks that are used in Spanish: the acute accent, diaeresis, tilde, and tittle.

examples.english:
—What’s a firulete?
—Pedigüeñería has the dot on the first “i”, the two dots on the “ü”, the hat on the “ñ” and the tilde on the final “í”! Those are firuletes!
examples.ref: 2007 April 16, Jordi Sierra i Fabra, El asesinato de la profesora de lengua (Duende Verde), Anaya Infantil y Juvenil, →ISBN, page 20:
examples.text:
—¿Qué es un firulete?
—¡Pedigüeñería tiene el punto de la primera «i», los dos puntos de la «ü», el sombrero de la «ñ» y la tilde de la «í» final! ¡Eso son firuletes!
examples.translation:
—What’s a firulete?
—Pedigüeñería has the dot on the first “i”, the two dots on the “ü”, the hat on the “ñ” and the tilde on the final “í”! Those are firuletes!

examples.english: pedigüeñería—is the word that has the four firuletes of our language; that is to say, the tittle of the i, the diaeresis of the u, the tilde of the ñ and the accent: i, ü, ñ, í.
examples.ref: 2018 August 7, Alejandra Santoy Sánchez, Palabrotas, palabrejas y otros bla bla blás, Alfaguara Infantil, →ISBN, page 200:
examples.text: pedigüeñería—es la palabra que tiene los cuatro firuletes de nuestro idioma; es decir, el punto de la i, la diéresis de la u, la virgulilla de la ñ y el acento: i, ü, ñ, í.
examples.translation: pedigüeñería—is the word that has the four firuletes of our language; that is to say, the tittle of the i, the diaeresis of the u, the tilde of the ñ and the accent: i, ü, ñ, í.

examples.english: In “pedigüeñería” appear the four firuletes that a term can have in our language: the tilde of the ñ, diaeresis over the ü, the accent mark and tittle over the i.
examples.ref: 2021 December 16, Roque Gambaro Royo, Demuestra que miento, Vision Libros, →ISBN, page 172:
examples.text: En “pedigüeñería” aparecen los cuatro firuletes que un término puede tener en nuestro idioma: la virgulilla de la ñ, diéresis sobre la ü, tilde del acento y el punto sobre la i.
examples.translation: In “pedigüeñería” appear the four firuletes that a term can have in our language: the tilde of the ñ, diaeresis over the ü, the accent mark and tittle over the i.

glosses: Any of the four diacritical marks that are used in Spanish: the acute accent, diaeresis, tilde, and tittle.
